summary: Request timeouts for long-context prompts with high max_tokens (504 / client-side timeout)
description: Issue summary: BrightLearn reports that API requests with long context windows and large max_tokens values are hitting client-visible timeouts (504 / client-side request timeout) or streaming disconnects. Impact: Several production endpoints for BrightLearn are failing ~10-15% of the time when generating long completions; customer workflows degrade and course-generation jobs are failing. Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-east-1. Occurs primarily on models configured for extended context (>= 16k).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use BrightLearn account API key against prod endpoint in us-east-1.
2) Submit a completion request with a ~12k token prompt and max_tokens set to 8k (streaming=false).
3) Observe long server-side generation (several tens of seconds to >120s) and then a 504 or client-side timeout.
4) Repeat with streaming=true: observe streaming disconnect after long initial delay or truncated responses.

metrics_summary: Observed spike starting 2026-03-02 09:30 UTC in BrightLearn tenant. Prior to spike: p95 latency ~1.8s for generation workloads. During spike: p50 ~18s, p95 ~95s, p99 >130s. Error rate (5xx/504) increased from 0.2% to 12% for affected endpoints. CPU/GPU utilization on dedicated pool increased to 92% with queue depth growth; autoscaler did not add capacity fast enough.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support: reproduced with BrightLearn's payload; confirmed timeouts only reproduce for long-context + large max_tokens. Hypotheses considered:
- KV cache memory pressure: large contexts increase KV cache and may push worker into slower fallback code path.
- Batching and head-of-line blocking: large requests occupy GPU long enough that subsequent requests queue and time out.
- Scheduler incorrect time estimation for long sequences leading to poor packing/too-large micro-batches.
- Autoscaling delay on Dedicated pool and conservative scale-up policy.
What we checked:
- Heap and GPU memory metrics on gw-12: no OOMs, KV cache peaked ~1.9GB but within quota.
- Serving-runtime logs show model step times increased non-linearly for sequence lengths >8k.
- Scheduler traces show requests flagged as "high-cost" but placed into same batch with small requests (head-of-line blocking).
- Autoscaler logs: scale event triggered but failed to add nodes due to quota error (error: "insufficient quota: p4-gpu-us-east") — follow-up with infra requested (INT-331).
Temporary tests run: pinned requests to dedicated worker pool with batch_size=1 reduced occurrence; enabling streaming reduced client-visible timeouts but increased partial responses.
Next steps planned:
1) SRE to clear quota / approve surge capacity (INT-331).
2) Patch scheduler to respect estimated cost and avoid batching long-context requests with short ones (PR linked).
3) Add request-level timeouts and early backpressure for very long max_tokens values with a customer-facing config.
4) Add more detailed long-sequence performance telemetry and regression alerting.
customer_communication:
2026-03-02 11:12 UTC: Acknowledge receipt and initial triage; asked for example request IDs and allowed us to run repros.
2026-03-02 13:05 UTC: Shared mitigation: recommend reducing max_tokens to <= 4096 or enable streaming=true; provided steps to pin to a smaller-context model variant temporarily.
2026-03-03 09:40 UTC: Informed customer we identified autoscaler quota bottleneck and are engaging infra to patch; offering temporary increase in request_timeout for their dedicated pool while permanent fix is implemented.
Customer asked for ETA on permanent fix and expressed that reductions in completion size are disruptive; we proposed staged rollout of scheduler change and will run canary tests with BrightLearn.
resolution:
Mitigation in progress. Short-term workarounds applied: (a) recommended customer reduce max_tokens or split prompts; (b) allowed temporary increase to client-side timeout for BrightLearn on dedicated pool; (c) provided guidance to enable streaming. Infra has been asked to clear GPU quota (INT-331). Engineering PR to scheduler (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821) is under review to avoid batching long-cost requests with short ones.
Planned permanent fixes: scheduler change + autoscaler policy update + improved long-seq telemetry and runbook. Will follow up with a post-incident note and regression alert once deployed.
